minimum_answer: Counterexample: a=[1,3], t=2. Initially l=0, r=1, m=0, a[0]=1<2 so l=m=0; loop repeats forever (l<r with l unchanged). Also a=[1,2], t=5 returns 1, not len(a)=2. Repair (half-open interval): l=0; r=len(a); while l<r: m=(l+r)//2; if a[m]<t: l=m+1 else: r=m; return l. Termination: each iteration either sets l=m+1>l or r=m<r, so r-l strictly decreases; O(log n) since interval halves. Boundary: maintain invariant that all i<l satisfy a[i]<t and all i>=r satisfy a[i]>=t. Initially l=0, r=len(a) satisfy it vacuously. If a[m]<t, then all i<=m have a[i]<t (sorted), so l=m+1 preserves the left part; if a[m]>=t, all i>=m have a[i]>=t, so r=m preserves the right part. On exit l=r, so every i<l has a[i]<t and every i>=l has a[i]>=t; hence l is the smallest index with a[i]>=t, or len(a) when t exceeds all entries. Duplicates are handled because the invariant uses strict/non-strict comparisons consistently.
